title: Vaccine efficacy in the immunosenescent elderly
bottleneck: Aging degrades every step of the vaccine response: dendritic cell antigen presentation, naive T cell output, B cell diversity, and antibody persistence. Older adults get weaker, shorter-lived protection from influenza, COVID-19, and pneumococcal vaccines, precisely when they need it most. Inflammaging further blunts vaccine-induced immunity.
why_it_blocks: Infectious disease is a leading killer of the oldest old, and the population is aging fastest where immune systems are weakest. If vaccines cannot protect the elderly, the single cheapest life-extending tool we have loses its power.
current_state: High-dose and adjuvanted (MF59, AS03) formulations plus booster schedules partially compensate, as used in high-dose flu vaccines. Research is shifting toward geroscience-informed adjuvants and pre-vaccination immune modulation, but no rejuvenation-based vaccine strategy is clinical.
